title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This guide consolidates Redwood Inference's standard hiring processes, candidate experience expectations, new-hire onboarding checklists, the performance and feedback cadence, and manager responsibilities. It is the single source of truth for people-ops, hiring managers, and people and product leaders. Use this document to run consistent, high-quality hiring and onboarding programs, reduce time-to-fill, and improve new-hire ramp and retention.

Key principles
- Candidate experience first: every interaction reflects Redwood's engineering-first, customer-centric culture.
- Speed with quality: target fast time-to-offer while preserving rigorous technical and culture evaluation.
- Manager accountability: hiring managers are owners of role definition, interview panels, and final calibration.
- Data-driven improvement: track offer acceptance, time-to-fill, and 90-day retention to iterate on process.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Purpose: Provide a repeatable, inclusive, and measurable process for sourcing, evaluating, and hiring top talent.

Stages and owners
1. Requisition creation (Owner: Hiring manager + People Ops)
   - Inputs: role brief, expected level, must-have skills, compensation band, preferred team start date.
   - SLA: req created in Greenhouse within 3 business days of manager approval.
2. Sourcing & screen (Owner: Recruiter)
   - Activities: outreach, inbound triage, recruiter screen to confirm fit and interest.
   - Target: 5-8 qualified candidate submissions per open role within 30 days.
3. Hiring manager screen (Owner: Hiring manager)
   - Focus: role expectations, culture fit, logistics. 30-minute interview.
4. Technical evaluation loop (Owner: Interviewers assigned by manager)
   - Typical interviews: coding/algorithms, system design, product/architecture, take-home assignment if needed.
   - Scorecard: role-fit, technical competency, problem solving, communication, ownership. Score 1-5 each.
5. Calibration & debrief (Owner: Hiring manager + panel)
   - Debrief within 48 hours of final interview. Use structured notes and scorecards.
6. Offer approval (Owner: Hiring manager + People Ops + Finance)
   - Approvals required: compensation band confirmation, sign-off from Finance for exceptions, executive approval for director+ roles.
   - SLA: approvals processed within 48 hours.
7. Offer extension & negotiation (Owner: Recruiter)
   - Standard offer window: 5 business days. Recruiter supports negotiation within approved band.
8. Acceptance, background checks, and onboarding kickoff (Owner: Recruiter + People Ops)
   - Background checks run after verbal acceptance. Onboarding plan and manager welcome sent within 2 business days.

Interview scorecard (example - use in Greenhouse template)
| Dimension | Description | Score (1-5) |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| Role fit | Matches core responsibilities and level | 1-5 |
| Technical skills | Problem solving, coding, system design | 1-5 |
| Ownership | Delivery mindset, cross-team collaboration | 1-5 |
| Communication | Clarity, empathy, feedback receptiveness | 1-5 |
| Culture add | Values alignment and diverse perspective | 1-5 |
| Overall recommendation | Strong hire / Hire / Consider / No hire | 1-5 |

Diversity, equity and inclusion
- All job postings must include a statement on inclusive hiring and reasonable accommodation contact.
- At least one underrepresented interviewer should be on the panel where possible.
- Require structured interview questions and scorecards to reduce bias.
- Track diversity metrics at application, interview, and offer stages monthly.

Hiring KPIs and targets
- Time-to-offer (req open -> offer extended): target 30 days.
- Time-to-fill (req open -> start date): target 45 days.
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 75%.
- 90-day retention of hires: target >= 90%.
- Interview-to-offer ratio: target <= 6 interviews per offer.

2) Offer & compensation process

Compensation banding and approvals
- Bands are published in the compensation matrix (People Ops maintains current bands).
- Hiring manager requests above-band offers via People Ops with a written business rationale. Finance approval required for any sign-on > 20% of midpoint.
- Equity grants use standardized templates; People Ops and Finance coordinate for senior hires.

Offer letter and negotiation best practices
- Always include role title, level, base salary, target equity, bonus (if eligible), sign-on, expected start date, and contingency (background check).
- Present the offer with total compensation context and promotion/leveling path.
- During negotiations, maintain internal offer equivalence and document concessions in the HRIS.

3) New-hire onboarding (first-day to 90-day ramp)

Goal: new hires reach independent contributor baseline as efficiently as possible and feel integrated into team and company culture.

First-day checklist (Owner: People Ops + Hiring manager)
- Pre-week: account creation (email, Slack, GitHub, internal tools), equipment shipped and tested, calendar invites for orientation.
- Day 0 (before start): welcome email with first-day logistics and primary contact.
- Day 1 must-complete items:
  1. People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, policies) - 60 minutes.
  2. Team welcome + manager 1:1 to set expectations - 60 minutes.
  3. IT and access verification - confirm repo and infra access.
  4. Security & compliance training - complete required modules.
  5. New-hire onboarding survey (quick pulse).

30/60/90-day ramp plan (Owner: Manager)
- 30-day goals: complete codebase walkthroughs, two small bugfix/features, join team rituals, and set development goals.
- 60-day goals: own a small project deliverable end-to-end, improve operational familiarity, and present a learnings doc.
- 90-day goals: ship meaningful impact, have a full performance check-in, and define long-term objectives.

Onboarding metrics and SLAs
- First-day completion of paperwork and training: 100%.
- 30-day onboarding checklist completion: target 90%.
- Manager should schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 90 days.

Buddy program and cross-functional introductions
- Assign a buddy from the team for the first 90 days. Buddy responsibilities: codebase tour, culture norms, and practical day-to-day questions.
- Schedule intro sessions with adjacent teams (Product, SRE, Security, Sales) in the first two weeks.

4) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and expectations
- Continuous feedback: weekly 1:1s between manager and direct report; document action items in manager notes.
- Formal performance reviews: semi-annual full-cycle reviews (mid-year and year-end) with goal-setting and calibration.
- Quarterly check-ins: manager and employee review progress on goals and adjust priorities.

Manager responsibilities
- Set clear, measurable objectives for direct reports tied to team and company goals.
- Provide regular coaching, unblock barriers, and document progress.
- Submit calibration notes and recommended ratings on schedule.
- Escalate performance concerns early to People Ops.

Calibration and rating guidelines
- Use a 5-point rating rubric with behavioral anchors (1: unsatisfactory, 3: meets expectations, 5: exceptional).
- Calibration panels are organized by People Ops; hiring managers must submit written justification for ratings 1 and 5.

Career conversations and promotion cycles
- Promotion readiness requires demonstrated impact, scope growth, and competency at the target level.
- Managers should run career conversations at least once per quarter and document progress in the career growth form.

Performance improvement plan (PIP)
- Trigger conditions: repeated missed expectations, sustained low ratings, or serious conduct issues.
- Typical timeline: 30-90 days based on gap severity.
- Steps: 1) manager documents concerns, 2) align on measurable expectations, 3) weekly 1:1s and progress reports, 4) People Ops oversight, 5) final assessment with possible outcomes: successful completion, extension, or separation.

5) Manager guide & best practices

1:1s and feedback
- Weekly 1:1 agenda template: wins, priorities, blockers, development, and feedback.
- Use real examples when giving feedback; close the loop on prior action items.

Onboarding new direct reports
- Week 1: align on role expectations, quick wins, and communication norms.
- Month 1: set goals, assign buddy, and ensure training/infra access.

Hiring as a manager
- Create clear role briefs that include measurable success criteria.
- Build diverse interview panels and ensure scorecards are used.
- Respect interview SLA: confirm panel availability within 3 business days of the candidate reaching the loop stage.

Manager escalation checklist (when performance or conduct concerns arise)
1. Document incidents and missed expectations.
2. Have an explicit coaching conversation and set measurable next steps.
3. Notify People Ops if no improvement in 2-3 weeks or for more serious issues.
4. Follow PIP process with People Ops involvement.

6) People policies quick reference

- Time off: managers approve PTO requests in the HRIS; encourage planning for major leaves 30 days in advance. Emergency leaves follow local statutory rules.
- Remote & hybrid work: Redwood supports distributed work; managers set team norms and in-office expectations with People Ops guidance.
- Code of conduct: expected behavior, anti-harassment policy, and reporting channels. Report incidents to people-ops@redwood.ai and security if needed.
- Confidentiality: employees must sign the confidentiality agreement at offer acceptance.
